diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume the oracle noise along the iterates satisfies the uniform conditional second-moment bound

issues.failure_explanation: The proofs of Lemma lem:optionB_stability, Lemma lem:contract_noise_bounded_iterates, Lemma lem:projSA_stability_template and all downstream rate/complexity results require a uniform conditional second-moment bound E[||T̂(v_t)-(r+Pv_t)||^2_∞ | F_t] ≤ σ^2 with a single deterministic constant σ^2. For the single-sample generative oracle T̂(v)(s)=r(s)+v(s̃_s) used in Algorithm alg:main_psa, the noise satisfies E[||ξ||^2_∞|F_t] ≤ C||v_t||^2_∞ (the noise is linear in v_t with random coefficients 1{s̃=s'}-P(s'|s)). The iterates are not shown to be almost-surely bounded: the deterministic recursion only gives ||v_{t+1}||_∞ ≤ (1+α_t)||v_t||_∞ + 2α_t R, i.e., worst-case polynomial growth, and the stability argument establishes only L^2 boundedness of e_t. Hence σ^2 is not a finite deterministic constant, so the hidden constants in the O(1/√T) bound are not well-defined for the algorithm as stated.

failure_location.quote: where the hidden constants depend on the contraction parameters and the oracle second moment bound.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either (a) prove the iterates are a.s. bounded (e.g., via a bootstrap closing E[||ξ||^2|F_t] ≤ C(1+||e_t||^2_q) and redoing the second-moment recursion), (b) weaken the oracle hypothesis to a state-dependent bound and re-derive the rate, or (c) modify alg:main_psa (e.g., project iterates onto a bounded set) so that uniform bounded noise holds. Each requires a contained but nontrivial argument beyond a routine edit.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed O(1/√T) convergence rate for Algorithm alg:main_psa and the end-to-end query-complexity corollaries are not established for the stated oracle; the entire stability/rate chain in Section 5.2 and its appendix is unsupported as applied to the given algorithm.
issues.title: Uniform oracle second-moment bound not verified for the stated single-sample generative oracle
issues.why_classification: The fix needs a contained nontrivial argument (bootstrap closing, weakened-hypothesis reanalysis, or an algorithm modification) but avoids new global proof architecture and preserves the advertised O(1/√T) rate and scope once done.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem thm:main_sa_rate claims E||[v_T]-[v*]||_q ≤ O(1/√T)+O(Nε_b) under only 'structural learning succeeds, weight estimation succeeds, γ̂<1'. The proof (and the formal version thm:projSA_rate_template) requires the additional hypothesis a=α(1-γ̂)>1/2 to bound Σ(t+t_0)^{2a-2} by O((T+t_0)^{2a-1}). For a≤1/2 the recursion yields m_T=Θ(T^{-2a}) and E||e_T||_q=Θ(T^{-a}) which grows strictly slower than T^{-1/2} (e.g., a=0.4 gives T^{-0.4}); the displayed constant 2^{a+1}αC_{q,∞}σ/√(2a-1) is not finite at a=1/2. So the claim of O(1/√T) without this hypothesis is false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis 'α(1-γ̂) > 1/2' to the statement of thm:main_sa_rate (and its informal corollary), matching the formal appendix; alternatively state the rate as O(T^{-min(α(1-γ̂),1/2)}) with the corresponding log correction at the boundary.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised O(1/√T) rate and the corresponding query budget T=Õ(1/ε^2) in the informal end-to-end corollary do not hold for parameter values with α(1-γ̂)≤1/2; for such parameters the rate degrades to O(T^{-α(1-γ̂)}).
issues.title: Rate theorem omits the required hypothesis α(1-γ̂) > 1/2 for the O(1/√T) rate
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard local step-size/contraction condition preserves the algorithm, the conclusion, the O(1/√T) rate (for allowed parameters), and the advertised multichain/periodic scope; no new lemma or construction is required since the formal appendix already carries the hypothesis.
